system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 4 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

A.

USE: 1 Triangle Tile and
1 Trapezoid Tile
MAKE: A 4-sided figure
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

Figure, described in words:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part A response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.

output.answer_1: Using 1 triangle tile and 1 trapezoid tile (4 triangle units total in the trapezoid-plus-triangle arrangement), I placed the triangle against one slanted side of the trapezoid so that they share one full edge. The resulting figure has 4 sides. On the grid, I drew the trapezoid (3 triangle units: top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) in the upper-right portion, and attached the single triangle tile to its slanted side in the lower-left portion, forming a 4-sided figure (a quadrilateral with sides of 1, 2, 2, and 2 units, or a parallelogram-like shape) drawn with bold outlines on the grid.
output.answer_2: Using 2 trapezoid tiles, I placed them so that their matching slanted edges meet along one full edge. Two trapezoids joined this way make a figure with 6 sides. On the grid I drew the first trapezoid (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit) in the upper-left portion and the second trapezoid (top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit, inverted) fitted against its right slanted side, outlining the combined 6-sided figure in bold lines on the grid.
output.answer_3: Using the same 2 trapezoid tiles, I rotated the second trapezoid and joined it to the first along a different pair of matching edges, so the outer boundary has 6 sides but a different arrangement of side lengths and angles from the figure in Part B. On the grid I drew the first trapezoid in the lower-left portion and the rotated second trapezoid attached along its slanted edge in a different orientation, outlining this different 6-sided figure in bold lines on the grid.
output.answer_4: Using 2 triangle tiles and 1 trapezoid tile (7 triangle units in total), I attached each triangle to a different side of the trapezoid so that all the pieces share edges and the outer boundary has 7 sides. On the larger grid I drew the trapezoid (3 triangle units) in the middle rows and attached one triangle along its bottom base and another along a slanted side, outlining the resulting 7-sided figure in bold lines on the grid.
